core_conclusion: VirTues is a marker-aware foundation model that embeds every protein channel through an ESM-2 protein language model and factorizes transformer attention into marker and spatial components, turning heterogeneous multiplex imaging cohorts into a single queryable virtual tissue atlas. One frozen backbone supports marker reconstruction, cell segmentation and typing, niche annotation, patient retrieval and biomarker discovery, with zero-shot transfer to unseen marker panels and unseen imaging technologies. In triple-negative breast cancer its learned multi-cellular spatial signatures predict anti-PD-L1 chemo-immunotherapy response (AUROC 0.823) and stratify disease-free survival in an independent cohort (c-index 0.628), outperforming published spatial biomarkers and clinical immune-ratio schemes.
why_it_matters: It removes the structural barrier of spatial proteomics - every study uses a different antibody panel and platform - by representing markers semantically rather than by index, so heterogeneous cohorts share one space. A single backbone replaces a chain of bespoke tools across the whole workflow, the discovered biomarkers are multi-cellular spatial programmes invisible to raw marker intensities, and they validate zero-shot on an independent cohort. The harmonized corpus, code and weights are released as reusable open infrastructure.
why_nature: A general platform capability rather than an incremental model; genuine architectural novelty (PLM marker tokens plus factorized attention breaking the fixed-panel assumption and quadratic channel scaling); a complete arc from self-supervised pretraining through interpretable attention to clinically actionable response and survival prediction; zero-shot generalization demonstrated across unseen markers, cohorts and imaging technologies rather than asserted; and a durable community resource extending the AI virtual cell agenda.
